verdict: Dover grew revenue 7.5% to $2.2B on double-digit growth in clean energy and climate, earning $2.50 a share — $2.88 before purchase-accounting and restructuring costs.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $2,234M, vs $2,078M a year ago (+7% organic)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: From continuing operations, vs $2.20 a year ago — total EPS was $2.47 after a small discontinued-operations loss

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: Up 10% YoY — excludes purchase-accounting and restructuring costs

kpis.label: Climate & Sustainability revenue
kpis.note: Up 18% YoY — the fastest-growing segment, helped by AI data-center cooling demand

segments.name: Clean Energy & Fueling
segments.note: Fueling equipment for gas stations and clean-energy fueling, plus vehicle wash and fluid handling. The largest segment, up 12%.

segments.name: Pumps & Process Solutions
segments.note: Pumps, compressors and process equipment for energy, chemical and life-science plants. Up 3%.

segments.name: Climate & Sustainability Technologies
segments.note: Refrigeration and cooling — including cooling for AI data centers and food retail. The fastest grower, up 18%.

segments.name: Imaging & Identification
segments.note: Printers and marking/coding equipment that put dates and codes on packaging. Up 2%.

segments.name: Engineered Products
segments.note: Bearings, lifting and towing gear and other engineered components. The only segment to shrink, down 2%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling Dover's products and running the company — its only operating-expense line. It includes purchase-accounting amortization and restructuring costs (see one-time items).

otherDetail: Other income of $14M plus $17M of interest income, less $29M of interest expense — a net $2M gain.
follow100Note: Segment rows add to $100.01 due to rounding. Kept-as-profit is earnings from continuing operations; total net earnings were $333M after a $3M discontinued-operations loss.

takeaways.title: Growth is broad — and orders are stronger
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 7.5% to $2,234M (+7% organic). Climate & Sustainability grew 18% and Clean Energy & Fueling 12%, helped by AI and power-generation demand. Bookings rose in all five segments and outpaced shipments, with much of the backlog due for delivery in 2027.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS vs the $2.50 GAAP figure
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings were $388M ($2.88 a share, +10%), excluding $46M of purchase-accounting expenses — mostly amortization of intangibles from past acquisitions — and $22M of restructuring costs, both pre-tax. GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $2.50.

takeaways.title: Buybacks and bolt-on deals continue
takeaways.text: Dover repurchased over $330M of its shares in the quarter and announced two small acquisitions, while investing in new capacity in its high-growth markets. Segment profit margin reached 24.3% of revenue, up from 24.2% a year ago.

oneTimers: Purchase accounting expenses of $46M pre-tax in the quarter — primarily amortization of intangible assets created by past acquisitions. Dover excludes these from adjusted earnings.
Restructuring and other costs of $22M pre-tax — headcount reductions, facility consolidations and site closures, and product-line exits. Also excluded from adjusted earnings.
A $3M loss from discontinued operations took total net earnings to $333M, below the $337M from continuing operations used in the flow above.
footerNote: Flow uses earnings from continuing operations ($337M); total net earnings were $333M after discontinued operations. Segment revenues are as reported in the release, rounded to $M — intersegment eliminations of $2M are absorbed in the rounding, and cost of revenue absorbs a $1M rounding difference so the lines add exactly.
